instruction.text: Task 1  Listen to this excerpt from a radio feature. You will hear three young people talking about loneliness and how they cope with their situation. Tap all statements that are made during the conversation.
instruction.sound: Task 1. Listen to this excerpt from a radio feature. You will hear three young people talking about loneliness and how they cope with their situation. Tap all statements that are made during the conversation.

atoms.a: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f13Us_chirp'>I get lonely. A lot.And it’s not like I’m, like, locked in a basement or whatever. I’m in group chats, I have coworkers, people see me.But… I don’t feel truly connected. I feel… present, but not… held. If that makes sense.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f12Us_chirp'>Mm. Yeah. Like you’re visible, but not known. I’ll be scrolling for ages and then I look up and I’m like— okay, I just watched other people liv. I didn’t actually talk to anyone.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3Us_chirp'>Yeah. Same. And people always assume school fixes it. Like, “You’re with people all day, how could you be lonely?”But sometimes it’s worse. ’Cause you’re surrounded and still feel… separate.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f13Us_chirp'>Exactly. And I do this thing: I’ll type a message like, “Hey, wanna hang?” and then I just… delete it.’Cause my brain goes: don’t be annoying. I just feel so needy and weird.I’m like: are they busy? are they judging me? did I say something cringe?And then I just… don’t send it.And then I’m alone and mad at myself for being alone.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f12Us_chirp'>Yep. Yep. I do that too.Or I’ll send, like, a meme instead, ’cause it’s safer.If they don’t reply, you can pretend it didn’t matter. It’s… dumb.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3Us_chirp'>No, it’s not dumb. It’s… a loop.And I see it everywhere online too— like, people our age just casually saying, “I feel empty,” or “I don’t really have anyone.”Not for attention. Just… stating it.And I’m like— okay, so it’s not just me. But also… why is it so common?</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f12Us_chirp'>I think we got used to distance. Like pandemic years, everything being online, staying inside, and then— boom— you’re supposed to be normal again.And I’m not sure we actually learned how.Also, like… especially guys, I think. Saying “I’m lonely” feels… weak.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3Us_chirp'>At my school it would turn into a joke. Like “same loll”, and then nobody actually… checks on you.And adults say, “Join a club,” or “Just talk to people,” and I’m like— okay, but what if you still feel invisible even when you do?</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f13Us_chirp'>Mm. Yeah. It’s not activities. It’s feeling… chosen.Like someone actually wants you there, not just… tolerates you.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f12Us_chirp'>Can I ask— when it gets heavy, what do you do?Like not bored-heavy. Real heavy.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f13Us_chirp'>Um… one small thing. I try to make it practical. Like— voice note someone. Text is too easy to hide behind. Voice is… more human. And I’ll say something simple, like: “Hey, I’m not doing great. Can we talk?” It’s awkward. But people are sometimes… nicer than you expect.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3Us_chirp'>Yeah. I do that with my cousin. Or I just… sit near my mom and go, “Can you stay in here for a minute?”Even if we don’t talk. Just… someone being there helps.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f13Us_chirp'>Yeah. Exactly. You don’t need a solution speech.You just need… a real person.And honestly, if there’s one thing I wish we’d get better at as a generation, it’s that: like, not deleting the message.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3Us_chirp'>Yeah. Not deleting it.</voice><voice voiceLang='en' voice='f12Us_chirp'>Mm-hm.Just… send it.</voice>

atoms.a: Scrolling through social media is described as …
b: ++watching other people live without actually talking to them.
a good way to stay emotionally close to friends.
something that replaces real conversations completely.
mostly relaxing and comforting.

atoms.a: Deleting messages before sending them is connected to …
b: ++fear of being annoying or judged.
not knowing how to use messaging apps.
having too many conversations at once.
not caring about other people’s reactions.

atoms.a: One speaker suggests that the pandemic …
b: ++made people used to distance and isolation.
improved social skills for most young people.
had no long-term effects on social behaviour.
mainly affected older generations.

atoms.a: When loneliness is mentioned at school, it is often …
b: ++turned into a joke instead of being taken seriously.
discussed openly in class.
handled by teachers immediately.
ignored because students are rarely lonely.

atoms.a: When loneliness feels “real heavy,” one speaker recommends …
b: ++sending a voice note instead of hiding behind text.
waiting until the feeling goes away.
posting about it on social media.
keeping busy with activities.

atoms.b:
One speaker says they delete messages because they feel annoying, needy and ((weird)).
According to one speaker, writing messages and then deleting them is not dumb, but can be described as a ((loop)) that makes loneliness worse.
During the pandemic, people got used to ((distance)) and being online all the time.
One speaker says that voice messages feel more ((human)) than text.
